input.brief: Clean&Process analytical workspace for one or two sources, showing contract results for prices, visual presentation, keywords, category opinions, evidence and partial coverage

style.name: Achromatic ledger
style.basis: 4 screens: a seller home, a per-agent insights page, a generated report, a settings page with usage numbers
style.idea: The chrome holds no colour at all; money and counts are set in ink, the one chart hue marks the screen's main data element, and the only other hue is a small signal where a figure changed.
style.colourBudget: under 1% coloured pixels; the chrome is ink, the one chart hue goes on the main data element, and the only other hue is a small change signal

font.second: Geist Mono, for IDs and keys only
font.note: 700 is for money figures only; every other number is 400-500.

style.signature: No brand colour anywhere in the chrome: the one primary action is near-black (a grey pill, #e5e5e5, is the secondary), the main data element (today's series, the booked bars, the current period) takes the one chart hue, #1d5fbf, and everything else is drawn in ink with the comparison or the part after the cursor in grey, zero balances are set in grey, and the only hue on the screen is a small triangle or a short coloured number where a figure changed.
identity: A ground from the product's world in place of #f8f8f8, one level off white and low in chroma: a stone (#f4f3f1) for a bakery or a shop, a sage (#f2f5f2) for a garden or a greenhouse, a blue-grey (#f2f4f7) for a ledger or a meter. Cards stay white; a warm tint stays under the cream check (saturation under about 15%).

The one chart hue (#1d5fbf, or the brand's own hue at 3:1 or more on white) on the screen's main data element: today's line, the booked bars, the current period's column, the margin that breaks. The chrome stays ink and the hue stays under 1% of the screen.
Every figure in Geist Mono, as the style's decision, so money and counts read as a ledger's columns while the text stays Geist. Lint and the inspector flag mono; give the reason in the report.
avoid: tinted cards or tinted KPI tiles
a coloured chart where one series in ink says it
a chart with no y-scale (the study's one example of this look hid magnitude behind hover and was flagged)
a grey pill as the only button for the screen's main job: in testing an Approve repeated in grey on every row left the screen without a primary
style.notes: The studied screens of this kind used 11-12px card radii, which §9.4 counts among the rare middle values; the library sets the tight pair (8 and 6) so the style lands on the bimodal rule. After testing, the chart hue moved from an unused third series colour onto the main data element: a screen whose only hue was a delta read as a kit.

shell.name: Open plane

numbers.sidebarWidth: 230-256 (230, 240, 256 in the study; 280 and 292 with a built-in icon rail)
numbers.separation: none, or one 1px hairline; the sidebar sits on the page ground or within 1-2% of it
numbers.activeItem: neutral grey pill, radius 6-12, inset 8-12px from the sidebar edges (#e9e9e9-#ededed)
numbers.canvas: fluid with a 24-64px gutter, or a centred 1100px column

shell.blueprint: The labelled sidebar sits on the page ground with nothing or one hairline between it and the canvas; there is no top bar, and the page header and cards sit straight on the ground about 32-36px from the top. Workspace or account switcher at the top of the sidebar, primary nav on a 34px pitch, groups under 12-13px sentence-case grey labels with 22-56px of air above, utilities and the user row pushed to the bottom. Cards are white on the off-white ground (or the sidebar is white with a 1px border on a #f9fafb canvas). The canvas is fluid with one gutter value, or a centred column for personal homes.
shell.phone: The sidebar folds into a 48px top bar holding the screen's name, a menu button that opens a full-screen sheet with the nav and the switcher, and at most one action. Content takes the full width with 16px margins.

pattern.name: Platform overview with a usage tray
pattern.blueprint: Sections stacked in one column about 48px apart, each with an 18/500 title on the left and a quiet action on the right ('View all', an outlined Refresh, a date-range button), and freshness in 14px grey after the title with a small status dot. First, a getting-started strip: one container split by 1px dividers into 4 equal cells (16/500 title, a 14px description, a grey arrow top right), shown until setup is done. Then the recent items table, capped at 4-5 rows on a 49px pitch: IDs in mono truncated to 8 characters plus an ellipsis with a copy icon, relative expiry in grey, rules that bleed 8px past the text column. Then usage: a #fafafa tray with 6px padding holding a KPI strip of 5 equal cells (a 14/500 label over a 24/400 value with a 14px unit suffix, '5 mins') and, 6px below, a chart card whose metric is chosen by the KPI cells themselves (the selected cell marked by a 2px rule or the active fill), never a second control repeating the KPI labels; the chart takes two-thirds of the width when its line is flat for most of the window, with the next answer beside it. Durations and timestamps in tabular figures. A missing value is a grey dash at label size, not '--' at value size.
pattern.phone: The getting-started strip becomes a 2 x 2 grid or a list; the table becomes two-line rows; the KPI strip a 2-column grid.

pattern.name: Bar list and ranking
pattern.blueprint: A 24/700 title with one factual stat chip beside the actions on the right; underline tabs on a 1px rule; a filter row of compound outlined groups that read as a sentence ('Date | Jun 14 - Jul 13 | Daily', 'Region | United States'), 28px tall and 8px apart. KPIs: as many equal columns as there are KPIs (four across, not four in a three-column grid that orphans one), tabular or mono values with fixed decimals. Then two equal panels, each with a 73px header (14/600 title, a 13px grey description, a dropdown that switches the panel's metric) over a full-bleed 1px rule: a sorted bar list (rows on a 64px pitch, a label line, then a 10px pill bar in one colour with no track, the value 5px after the bar's end, the longest bar about 88% of the width) and a ranking table (53px rows, rules inset to the padding, a rank, a 16px logo, a soft chip on the user's own row, values right-aligned). Do not fix a panel's height so its last row is cut off (flagged).
pattern.phone: KPIs in a 2 x 2 grid; panels stack; the bar list keeps its bars at full width.

pattern.name: Object header and a six-column grid
pattern.blueprint: The page header is the object itself: one card (88px, 14px padding) holding a 50x62 cover, the 18/600 name with 28px icon buttons beside it (open, copy, share), a 13px grey meta line (date, time, place) and outlined 36px actions on the right. Under it, underline tabs on a full-width 1px rule, then a 36px row with a segmented time range on the left and a refresh button on the right. The body is one 6-column grid with one gutter (14px) in both directions whose spans change by row while every edge lands on the same lines: 3 KPI tiles of 2 columns, the main chart in 4 columns beside a side chart in 2, two progress cards of 3, a full-width trend of 6. Give the widest card to the screen's question, and do not give 824px to one ring and one legend row (flagged).
pattern.phone: The header card keeps cover, name and meta, with actions in a kebab; every grid item takes the full width in the same order.
